newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Michael Meacher, the spokesman for Britain's Environment Minister, warned yesterday that Australia would face international condemnation if it did not sign an international agreement on targets for greenhouse gas emission reductions. Prime Minister John Howard will argue the case for Australia's opposition to the treaty to British counterpart Tony Blair when the leaders meet in London tomorrow. Page 1.

In recent years industrial property trusts have established a A$1 billion presence on the Australian Stock Exchange and investors now value them highly. To take advantage of this, leading finance companies Legal & General, Axiom Funds Management and Mercntile Mutual are planning a float of over A$400 million in industrial property in new trusts. Page 1.

The liquidator of Bond Corp, Ernst & Young partner Richard England, has launched civil action against Bond family members and others over the "Alan Bond collection". England claims that 14 paintings from the collection were sold in "sham" deals in Decembr 1989 at much less then their actual values. Page 1

The Federal Government has taken a new approach to the tax reform debate, with Prime Minister John Howard and Federal Treasurer Peter Costello saying that tax reform would ease the financial burden on the PAYE system. The claim came as Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley reaffirmed Labor's opposition to any GST tax. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

National Party federal president Don McDonald is anxiously awaiting the Federal Government's draft legislation on the High Court's Wik decision. Two thirds of the pastoral area owned by him and his brother is currently subject to native title claims. Page 1.

Tricia Kemp-Elliott, the former head of the Jabil Centre at the Australian National University, has returned to settle in her home town of Wilcannia, in far west NSW. When she was 12-years-old Kemp-Elliott won dux at the local Catholic Primary school, and she remembers the local postmaster claiming that "a coloured girl" should not have received the award. Page 1.

The latest statistics reveal that long-term unemployment rose to 16 per cent over the past year and the jobless rate increased to twice the national average in some areas. The number of people unemployed for over a year was 239,500 - 33,100 higher than in May last year. Page 1.

Federal Cabinet approved an overhaul of the youth welfare system yesterday that will see approximately 25,000 16 and 17-year-olds lose their unemployment benefits. Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman stated the reforms will also see nearly 50,000 young people aged between 18 and 21 lose their unemployment benefits or receive a lower payment. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Federal Government has introduced a major social security policy change which will force families to take greater financial responsibility for the care of their children. Under reforms approved yesterday by the Federal Government unemployment benefit will be abolished for under 18-year-olds, and accessibility to benefits for those aged between 18 and 20 will be decided on the basis of their parents' income. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard is set to defend Australia's reputation during his overseas trip. Following international criticism on human rights issues Howard has recently increased his criticism of One Nation Leader Pauline Hanson, comparing her to former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke and the leader of France's far-right National Front, Jean-marie Le Pen. Page 1.

The NSW Government's controversial bed tax and the poker machine tax increase were passed in the Legislative Council last night following support from the majority of the seven cross-bench members. The tourism and licensed club industries said they would campaign against the taxes until the next State election, due in 1999. Page 1.

Reverend Fred Nile, of the Call to Australia Party, named NSW Council for Civil Liberties head John Marsden in State Parliament yesterday as a defendant in a civil action suit concerning the alleged sexual abuse of an eight-year-old. Nile asked Attorney-general Fred Shaw if he was aware of the action and if it had been brought to the attention of the Royal Commission into the NSW Police Service. Page 2.
THE AGE

Under a shakeup of the youth welfare system, the Federal Government will restrict the dole to those over 18 and make parents more financially responsible for their children until they reach the age of 21. The new system will combine previously separate pyments such as Austudy, Newstart, the youth training allowance, sickness allowance and upper-teen family payments, and those aged between 16 and 21 will be assessed on their parents' income, even if they no longer live at home. Page 1.

The Federal and Vic Governments will investigate the circumstances surrounding the death of a infant who could have been taking part in the vaccine trials being conducted between 1967 and 1970 in orphanages and baby homes. The death was referred to at a 1972 international conference, the International Symposium on Influenza Vaccines for Men and Horses, by a Commonwealth Serum Laboratories vaccine researcher. Page 1.

Police yesterday conducted a third day of intensive searching for missing toddler Jaidyn Leskie, who disappeared from a house in Narracan Drive, Newborough, between 2am and 3am on Sunday morning. Police say they still hold out hopes for his safety, but they are considering other possibilities. Page 1.

The Kennett Government's front bench could change drastically in the future with up to one-third of ministers, including Conservation Minister Marie Tehan and Attorney-General Jan Wade, not expected to contest the next election. Although the next election cannot be held until March 1999, pre-selections will begin in one year's time and jockeying for positions has already begun. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
